summary: API Gateway 5xx amplification from connection-slab fragmentation and scheduler latency during tenant burst
description:
Issue summary: NoteStream reported a rapid increase in 5xx responses (502/503/504) beginning 2026-03-12 18:32 UTC during a scheduled bulk ingestion. Impact: production traffic for NoteStream (dedicated pool) experienced elevated error rates (~18% 5xx for 20 minutes) and increased tail latency causing customer throttles and several client timeouts. Environment: prod, us-east, dedicated GPU pool.

Observed behavior: API Gateway began returning 502/503 in waves correlated with spikes in connection queue length and a burst of ephemeral worker churn. The serving runtime reported repeated short-lived OOMs and scheduler logs show latency spikes in task assignment. KV-cache metrics show increased shard contention and growth of pending prefetch queues.

Expected behavior: Traffic should remain within acceptable error floor (<0.1% 5xx) using the tenant's reserved capacity and fallback routing should continue serving requests with minimal errors.

Steps to reproduce (approximate):
1) Customer triggered a large multi-tenanted embedding upload (~1.2M vectors) which hit the dedicated ingestion route.
2) Traffic pattern: sustained 1000 rps with occasional 5k rps bursts over 10s windows.
3) Within 1-2 minutes of bursts, api-gateway accept queue grows, keepalive pool exhibits high turnover, and runtime scheduler delays tasks > 250ms.

Logs / dashboards referenced:
- Support dashboard (internal): /dashboards/incidents/SUP-404321
- Grafana: apigw/conn-queue-length (spike), scheduler/assignment-latency (tail spike), runtime/gpu-memory-alloc-failures (brief increases).
- Customer-provided client logs: multiple HTTP 502 with upstream-reset messages and intermittent TLS handshake failures.

Immediate customer impact: degraded UX for NoteStream embedding uploads; retries caused higher load and amplified the condition.
comments: 2026-03-12 18:45 - Maya Patel (Support): Acknowledge issue with NoteStream. Collected initial logs and asked SRE to triage. First response provided to customer; they confirm the high-volume embed job and are pausing further uploads.

2026-03-12 18:53 - Jamal Rivera (SRE): Observed apigw accept-queue collapse across several hosts and high connection turnover. Correlating with scheduler lag and kvcache shard hotlocks. Tentatively rolling partial ingress route weight away from the affected hosts.

2026-03-12 19:07 - Ethan Park (Oncall Eng): Deployed ingress soft-shed policy for NoteStream traffic and increased keepalive pool size on the affected frontends as a mitigation. Asking customer to resume small test batch.
2026-03-12 19:20 - NoteStream Support Contact (Customer): Confirmed error rate dropped to ~1.2% after soft-shed and smaller test batch. Full ingestion still blocked pending further investigation.

2026-03-13 09:12 - Priya Menon (ServRuntime): Reproduced scheduler tail latency when connection slab fragmentation reaches >80% fragmentation_ratio. Opening an engineering investigation to look into allocator behavior and prefetch lock ordering.

2026-03-13 12:30 - Ethan Park (Oncall Eng): Added SUP-472901 and INT-830 to linked_issues for further incident correlation. Preparing post-incident rollback plan for a kernel change that landed yesterday.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Connection-slab fragmentation on frontends reduces effective available sockets, causing keepalive churn and upstream connection resets which amplify apigw 5xx responses.

Hypothesis 2: Scheduler latency under high accept-queue pressure leads to delayed runtime task assignment; combined with kv-cache hotlocks this causes transient GPU OOMs when multiple prefetches race.
Metrics observed: accept_queue_depth (10x baseline), conn_slab_fragmentation_ratio (0.84), scheduler_assignment_p95 (420ms), runtime_gpu_alloc_failures (spike at incident start).

Correlated events: a small kernel-level allocator tweak was rolled out in us-east yesterday (deploy-id: deploy-2026-03-11-22). Candidate for regression testing. Related PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/5120.

Repro attempt: Synthetic load reproduces accept-queue growth and fragmentation but full OOM chain only reproduced when combined with a high prefetch rate from the KV cache. Adding randomized prefetch jitter in tests reduces error amplification.
resolution: Mitigation: temporary ingress weight adjustment and keepalive pool parameter bump reduced 5xx rate to acceptable level. Engineering reverted the allocator tweak in us-east and scheduled a targeted fix for prefetch lock ordering. Customer resumed ingestion under guidance.
resolution_notes: Timeline: 2026-03-12 19:00 - ingress weight shift; 19:10 - keepalive pool bump; 2026-03-13 02:14 - revert allocator tweak; 2026-03-13 11:00 - schedule fix for kvcache prefetch locking (PR opened).

Customer communication: Notified NoteStream of temporary mitigations and requested staged resume of uploads. Confirmed final verification run at 2026-03-13 11:45 with zero 5xx over 30 minutes for 300 rps test.

Permanent fix plan: update allocator to avoid fragmentation under high churn, add scheduler backpressure signal to ingress to avoid accept-queue collapse, and introduce randomized prefetch jitter per-tenant in serving-runtime. Target ETA: 2026-03-25 for merged PRs and canary rollout.
Postmortem: Drafting postmortem and runbook updates for conn-slab detection and scheduled prefetch throttles. Linking to incident page when complete.
